title: Fuyan Cave human teeth, Daoxian, China
summary: Forty-seven human teeth from Fuyan Cave in Daoxian County, Hunan, southern China, were reported in Nature in 2015 and described as the earliest unequivocally modern humans in southern China. The teeth are more than 80,000 years old and may be as old as 120,000 years, which suggests modern humans reached China well before settling in Europe.

uncertainty.note: Years before present in the sources are written here as negative calendar years without subtracting 1950; the sources give rounded ages. Leiden and Sci.News both give "more than 80,000 years" with a possible maximum of 120,000 years.

as_recorded.value: more than 80,000 years old, although they may be as old as 120,000 years

when.display: more than 80,000 and up to 120,000 years ago

where.modern_name: Fuyan Cave, Tangbei Village, Daoxian County, Hunan Province, China
where.historical_name: Limestone cave in what is now southern China; no polity applies

importance.justification: Argued to show modern humans in southern China well before Europe, bearing on the timing of dispersal out of Africa.
